# DATA PKT Infra & Geomatics (DATAPKT)

> Drone survey, mapping, GIS and design company based in Gurugram, Haryana, India, founded on 14 September 2020. We survey, map and design for infrastructure projects; we do not build them. Empanelled with the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) in three zones for monthly drone survey work. DIPP-recognised start-up. Legal name: DATAPKT Private Limited.

## What we do
- Drone and DGPS topographic surveys for highways, roads and expressways
- Railway and metro surveys, including Engineering Scale Plans (ESP), yard plans and drainage plans
- Survey and design inputs for Detailed Project Reports (DPRs)
- Drone thermal (infrared) inspection of solar power plants and electrical assets
- Transmission line route surveys and substation site surveys
- Water resources surveys and bathymetry for canals, rivers and reservoirs
- Photogrammetry: orthomosaics, digital terrain and surface models, contours and volumes
- LiDAR survey and classified point clouds
- GIS mapping and data processing, including remote GIS work for clients outside India
- Aerial videography and monthly progress videos for projects

## Sectors
Highways and roads, railways and metro, power and solar, water resources, urban planning, mining, oil and gas, environment, agriculture, archaeology, public safety, manufacturing and wildlife.

## Where we work
Projects across India from our Gurugram office. Remote GIS data processing for clients outside India.

About DATA PKT

## We survey, map and design the ground India builds on.
DATA PKT Infra & Geomatics is a drone survey, mapping, GIS and design company based in Gurugram, Haryana. Since 2020 our pilots, surveyors, GIS analysts and engineers have worked on highways, railways, solar plants, power lines, canals and mines across India.

### What we do
We collect accurate data about the ground and the assets on it, and turn it into drawings, GIS layers and reports that engineers and owners can use. We survey, map and design for infrastructure projects; we do not construct them.
- Drone and DGPS topographic surveys for highways, roads, railways, canals and industrial sites
- Engineering Scale Plans, yard plans and DPR survey inputs for railway and road projects
- LiDAR surveys and classified point clouds, including terrain under vegetation
- Photogrammetry: orthomosaics, terrain and surface models, contours and volumes
- Drone thermal inspection of solar PV plants and electrical assets
- Transmission line route surveys and substation site surveys
- Water resources surveys and bathymetry for canals, rivers and reservoirs
- GIS mapping and data processing , including remote processing for clients outside India
- Aerial videography and monthly progress videos for projects

### How a project runs
- Scope: we agree the area or corridor, the accuracy needed, the coordinate system and the deliverables.
- Plan: flight plans, ground control layout and the permissions the site needs under India's drone rules.
- Capture: our pilots fly the site while surveyors measure ground control with DGPS.
- Process: the GIS team builds the orthomosaic, terrain models and point clouds and checks accuracy against independent checkpoints.
- Deliver: drawings, GIS layers and reports in the formats your team uses, with an accuracy report.

Roads & Highways DATAPKT enables tracking and monitoring of a road network's condition throughout all phases of development, from construction to maintenance once it has been operationalized. Drones can be employed for corridor modelling, bridge inspection, pavement condition mapping, and road distress tracking in the roadways sector. Data collection via aerial surveying reduces total expenses by substantially minimising the number of site inspections needed to record highway conditions as well as challenges in real time with greater precision.
Railways & Metros UAV technology has the ability to conduct real-time monitoring, video streaming, and drone-based surveillance of crucial railway assets. DATA PKT makes it simpler to survey areas that might be unsafe for human inspectors, such as near live electrical wires or tracks. Drones assist in the creation of 3D models of stations and landscapes for site visualisation, as well as contour maps for areas where new railway lines are proposed in order to create accurate plans.
Energy The DATAPKT predictive algorithm offers a comprehensive visual site inspection of transmission lines, solar fields, wind farms, and hydropower projects. Drones equipped with high-resolution, infrared, thermal cameras have the potential to reduce transmission and distribution losses, lower maintenance costs, and detect anomalies in advance. Drone surveys can detect faults in power lines in real time, assisting with repairs and maintenance and drastically reducing power outages and costs.
Mining DATA PKT drone observations lead to more effective mining operations by rendering assistance such as managing inventory, hotspot detection, and stockpile management. Drone aerial images can be used to generate digital terrain models, digital surface models, and 3D terrain models of mining sites. UAVs reduce delays and make it easier to detect the depth and elevation of mining blocks, making highly toxic, difficult-to-reach areas accessible. High-resolution images with data pkt drones make the inspection, mapping, and monitoring of harsh terrain possible.
Oil & Gas Drones from DATAPKT can inspect, monitor, map, and deliver in-depth reports of oil and gas fields. Our drone pilots can conduct online external and internal visual inspections of refinery flare stacks. As a result of their ability to access far-flung or challenging locations, drones are used for remote surveillance during routine operations as well as in emergency situations. UAVs can be used to conduct rapid, frequent, and real-time aerial inspections to protect asset integrity by monitoring miles of pipelines for gas emissions or leaks.
Water Resources UAV technology aids in the monitoring of rivers and the formation of precise and reliable landscape models for their preservation and restoration. Drones used for dam inspection, irrigation canal management, river route mapping, wetland conservation, as well as other purposes help to safeguard scarce water resources while also allowing for more efficient water use. The use of drones to detect potential risks towards the sustainability of freshwater resources is critical for taking timely action and securing future generations.
Urban Planning DATA PKT enables planners and developers obtain streamlined data from complex urban areas. UAVs equipped with 360-degree view 4k resolution cameras produce high-quality 3D aerial images and orthophoto maps, making project drafting and implementation quite cost-effective. In order to examine the current social and ecological conditions of the site using drone technology, DATA PKT assists in producing high-quality and accurate detailed reports of environmentally hazardous areas.
Public Safety DATA PKT drones can conduct real-time surveillance of protests and public unrest sites by keeping an eye on the ground situation to detect threats to public safety. UAVs assist in tracking and monitoring the movements of people by conducting aerial surveys in high-risk areas. Drones can fly in all weather conditions, assisting in the saving of lives during disasters and natural hazards such as floods, tsunamis, and earthquakes among others. Drones can assist with the delivery of crucial and essential articles in difficult terrain.
Manufacturing DATAPKT's services help to streamline manufacturing services by keeping a real-time record of on-site activities. By accelerating inspection and monitoring of large areas in a short amount of time, DATAPKT AI-powered solutions contribute to cost reduction, increased speed, and scalability of operations. Among other things, sophisticated drone technology assists the manufacturing industry in monitoring assets, increasing personnel safety, and speeding up inventory checks. Drones boost manufacturing units output and productivity while also improving their efficiency and security.
Wildlife Tracking and mapping out the movements of wildlife, especially those of endangered species, using UAVs helps in-situ conservation. DATAPKT can monitor the wildlife ecosystems of critical animals without disrupting their native environment. UAVs aid in the accurate population counting of species and help with aerial imagery capture, both of which are important for the study of important wildlife. By keeping an eye on the forest's health, landscapes, and tree cover, drones also contribute to the sustainable conservation of biodiversity.
Agriculture DATAPKT promotes and conserves the agricultural sector by offering precise and reliable field mapping and assisting farmers in identifying any irregularities in the field. Farmers can practise smart farming by using drones to monitor their crops. Using drones for comprehensive field surveys facilitates producers in addressing soil and crop health while improving crop production efficiency. This aids in the optimization of production and the selection of suitable crops for the field conditions. Drones assist in cost reduction, improved time management, and better opportunities for farmers.
Archaeology The sensors used in DATAPKT systems provide an in-depth evaluation of historical sites and aid in the documentation of significant archaeological monuments. Drones aid in the accurate mapping of protected sites, making features and structures easily identifiable. This helps archaeologists in their future research regarding the conservation and preservation of archaeological sites.

### Frequently asked questions

Q: What does DATA PKT do?
DATA PKT Infra & Geomatics is a drone survey, mapping, GIS and design company based in Gurugram, Haryana. We survey and map infrastructure such as highways, railways, solar plants, power lines, canals and mines, and turn that data into drawings, GIS layers and reports. We survey, map and design for projects; we do not build them.

Q: Where does DATA PKT work?
Our office is in Sector 48, Gurugram, and our survey teams work on projects across India. Our GIS team also processes data remotely for clients outside India.

Q: Is DATA PKT empanelled with NHAI?
Yes. DATA PKT is empanelled with the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) in three zones for monthly drone survey work.

Q: What do I get from a drone survey?
Typical deliverables are a georeferenced orthomosaic, a digital surface model (DSM), a digital terrain model (DTM), contours, CAD drawings and GIS layers, plus volumes or progress reports where the project needs them. The exact set is agreed at the start of each project.

Q: How do I request a quote?
Call +91 8448559100, email consult@datapkt.com, or use the enquiry form on this site. Share the site location, area or corridor length, and the outputs you need, and we will reply with a scope and quote.

## Drone Survey for Highways and Roads
Pre-Construction
Under Construction
O & M
We offer a range of valuable services in the pre-construction phase of highway development, providing efficient data collection, analysis, and monitoring capabilities. Here are some of the key services we can offer:
Detailed Project Report (DPR)

#### Surveying and Mapping
Drones equipped with high-resolution cameras and LiDAR (Light Detection and Ranging) sensors can quickly survey large areas to create detailed topographic maps and 3D models. This data helps engineers and planners understand the terrain, identify potential obstacles, and plan the highway route more accurately.

#### Site Inspection
Drones can conduct regular site inspections to monitor progress, identify potential safety hazards, and ensure compliance with design specifications. They can capture high-definition images and videos of the construction site from various angles, providing valuable visual documentation for project stakeholders.

#### Earthwork Monitoring
By flying over construction sites, drones can track earthmoving activities, measure stockpile volumes, and monitor cut and fill operations. This data helps project managers optimize resource allocation, track progress, and detect deviations from the project schedule

#### Best Route Analysis
DATA PKT assists its clients in selecting from among the various proposed routes the best alignment from point A to point B, connecting cities, populations, and industries. We collect site information using UAVs and convert it into othomosaic maps, digital elevation models and contours, which help check and resolve conflict with proposed and existing structures. We digitize the revenue map and estimate the cost of land and analyse the expenditure of the construction with the stockpile volume, obstacles , ground feature measurement and estimated circles rates to offer a cost efficient way to construct a highway.

#### Progress Monitoring
We capture and process the raw drone images to generate orthophotos, which are geometrically corrected and distortion-free images of the construction site. We use photogrammetry software to stitch together the images and create orthophotos with high accuracy and resolution. Compare orthophotos captured at different time points to identify changes and progress in the construction work and determine the work completion percentage and expected time of work completion.

#### Video Project Report ( VPR )
Drones from DATA PKT capture aerial photogrammetric data once each month and generate a customised video project report with key project completion rates and site surveillance information. Monthly comparative reports are also provided to assist in detecting new encroachments and buildings being developed on the site.

#### Utility Shifting
l surveys to capture detailed images of the construction site, focusing on areas where utility lines are being relocated or adjusted. Analyze the drone imagery to track the progress of utility shifting, ensuring compliance with project timelines and minimizing disruptions to services. Identify any potential conflicts or safety hazards arising from utility relocations and promptly address them to prevent delays and accidents. Generate comprehensive reports documenting the status of utility shifting activities and facilitating coordination between construction teams and utility providers for efficient project management.

#### Electronic Record Generation
Drone-generated electronic records are exceedingly accurate and of high quality. It acts as trustworthy proof for highway construction businesses to receive prompt reimbursement from the government and insurance companies in the event of a review.

#### Higher Transparency and Visibility
To boost transparency and consistency and make use of cutting-edge technology, the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI), which falls under the ministry of Road, Transport, and Highways.

### Operations And Maintenance
Road laying alone does not mark the end of a highway construction process; rather, it is the beginning of a continuous process that necessitates ongoing operations and maintenance. The following services are provided by DATA PKT to its clients to assist them in maintaining their assets:
Drones from DATA PKT gather high-quality aerial data and convert it into 3D point clouds to aid in mapping roads in need of repair. Our image processing software uses this for pothole detection and encroachment identification using comparative monthly video project reports. The prompt discovery of any abnormalities after the construction of roadways and highways aids in the protection of lives that might otherwise be lost due to unsafe road conditions.
We capture high-resolution aerial images of highway right-of-way areas. Conduct regular flights to monitor for encroachments such as illegal structures, vegetation overgrowth, or unauthorized activities. Analyze the drone imagery to identify encroachments and assess their extent and impact on highway safety and functionality. Generate detailed encroachment reports with annotated images to document findings and inform appropriate authorities for corrective action. Utilize this proactive approach to maintain the integrity of highway right-of-way and ensure compliance with legal regulations.
Corridor mapping with our UAV services revolutionises data capture along linear features. We offer cost-effective, efficient, and precise mapping solutions. From flight planning to data processing, we provide high-resolution imagery for diverse applications like transportation planning, asset management, and emergency response. This streamlined approach enhances safety, reduces costs, and enables informed decision-making. With ongoing advancements, UAV technology promises continued growth and valuable insights for infrastructure management.

The dynamic nature of our cutting-edge drone technology revolutionizes the way engineers assess bridges, offering unparalleled versatility and comprehensive insights into their structural integrity and condition. These advanced drones can navigate and inspect bridges from every conceivable angle and perspective, providing engineers with a holistic view of their performance and potential vulnerabilities. By leveraging their small size and swift movement capabilities, drones have become indispensable tools for inspecting and surveying remote areas, where traditional methods would be impractical or unsafe.
Equipped with high-resolution cameras and state-of-the-art sensors, these drones capture sharp, detailed photos, and videos that offer a wealth of valuable information for engineers and infrastructure managers. From capturing close-up shots of intricate bridge components to providing sweeping panoramic views of entire structures, drones deliver visual data that enhances the accuracy and efficiency of bridge inspections. Moreover, their ability to access hard-to-reach areas ensures that no aspect of bridge infrastructure goes unchecked, enabling engineers to identify potential issues and address them proactively. By harnessing the power of drone technology, engineers can optimize maintenance strategies, prioritize repairs, and ensure the safety and longevity of critical transportation infrastructure for years to come.
Incorporate drones equipped with cutting-edge aerial imaging capabilities into the post-construction phase of the highway project to conduct a thorough survey of the surrounding area. Capture high-resolution images encompassing the entire vicinity to provide detailed coverage for accurately counting and mapping existing trees. Utilize advanced image processing techniques to analyze the drone imagery and precisely identify suitable locations for tree plantation along the highway corridor, considering factors such as soil quality, sunlight exposure, and proximity to water sources. This meticulous analysis ensures the identification of optimal sites that will foster the growth and sustainability of newly planted trees.
Furthermore, generate comprehensive reports that outline the tree count, species distribution, and proposed plantation sites, providing stakeholders with valuable insights to facilitate informed decision-making and prioritize environmental stewardship initiatives. By implementing proactive measures to enhance green infrastructure and biodiversity, the project can mitigate the environmental impact of highway construction and contribute to the long-term sustainability of the surrounding ecosystem.

### Deliverables

### Detailed Project Reporting (DPR)
DPR offers comprehensive services like surveying, site inspection, earthwork monitoring, and best route analysis, optimizing highway construction for longevity, cost-effectiveness, and sustainability, ensuring efficient project management and high-quality infrastructure development.

### DTM
DTM's (Digital Terrain Model) are detected using aerial photography at low heights with a geometrically calibrated camera. This enables the drone to obtain all heights of a surveyed terrain.Generating Digital Terrain Models (DTM) for highways with drones provides detailed elevation data essential for accurate design and construction planning.

### Contour Mapping
Drone data enables accurate contour mapping for highways, providing essential topographic insights for efficient road design and construction. This technology streamlines the process, enhancing project planning and execution while ensuring optimal route alignment and drainage management.

### Orthomosaic

### Frequently asked questions

Q: Can a drone survey replace a conventional topographic survey for a highway DPR?
For most corridors, a drone survey tied to DGPS ground control points gives the base topography for a DPR faster than a fully manual survey. Areas under dense tree cover, structures and cross-drainage details are usually completed with DGPS or total station on the ground. The two methods are normally combined rather than one replacing the other.

Q: What outputs does a highway drone survey give?
An orthomosaic of the corridor, a terrain model (DTM), contours, the existing road and features in CAD, and cross-sections where needed. During construction, the same corridor can be flown again for progress monitoring and video reports.

Q: How is progress on an under-construction highway monitored with drones?
The same stretch is flown at regular intervals, usually monthly, and each flight is compared with the last. This gives a visual record of progress, quantities moved and issues on site that can be shared with the authority and the contractor.

Q: Does DATA PKT work with NHAI?
Yes. DATA PKT is empanelled with NHAI in three zones for monthly drone survey work.

### Engineering scale Planning
An engineering scale plan in railways is a detailed, technical drawing that illustrates the design and layout of railway infrastructure. This includes tracks, signals, stations, bridges, tunnels, and other related components. The purpose of such a plan is to provide a precise, scaled representation of how the railway system will be constructed and operated.

### Frequently asked questions

Q: What is an Engineering Scale Plan (ESP)?
An Engineering Scale Plan is a scaled drawing of a railway station yard or section that shows tracks, points and crossings, platforms, buildings and other structures in their true positions. It is used to plan yard remodelling, new lines and other works. Drone and LiDAR surveys provide the accurate base data an ESP is drawn on.

Q: Why use drones for railway surveys?
A drone covers a yard or a long section of track quickly without staff working on the line for long periods, which improves safety and reduces block time. Survey-grade accuracy comes from ground control and RTK or PPK positioning.

Q: What railway deliverables can be produced?
Engineering Scale Plans, yard plans, drainage plans, longitudinal and cross sections, orthomosaics, terrain models, and GIS layers of railway land and assets.

Q: Can metro corridors be surveyed in dense cities?
Yes, subject to flight permissions. In crowded urban areas the drone survey is planned around permitted zones and timings and is combined with ground survey where flying is restricted.

## Engineering Scale Plans (ESP) and DPR Surveys

In summary, our UAV data service supports railway engineering scale planning by providing accurate, detailed, and real-time information that enhances the efficiency, safety, and cost-effectiveness of railway operations and infrastructure development.

### What an Engineering Scale Plan shows
An Engineering Scale Plan (ESP) is the railway's master drawing of a station yard or section, drawn to scale with every feature in its true position. Engineering, signalling, traction and operating departments all work from it, and it is the base on which yard remodelling, new lines and other works are planned, checked and approved. An ESP prepared from a drone survey typically shows:
- Track: running lines, loops and sidings, track centres, and the kilometrage along the section
- Points and crossings: every turnout with its position and direction
- Platforms and passenger structures: platform lengths and edges, foot-over-bridges, ramps, shelters and station buildings
- Crossings of the line: level crossings, road over-bridges and road under-bridges
- Traction and signalling: OHE masts and portals, signals and cabins
- Bridges, culverts and drains , with their position on the section
- Buildings and land: goods sheds, service buildings, quarters, boundary walls and fencing, and the railway land boundary
- Levels: spot levels and contours for drainage, formation and earthwork

### Where railways use ESPs and drone surveys

### How we prepare an ESP
- Scope and permissions: the yard limits, the chainage and the drawing standard are fixed with the railway, and flights are cleared with the station and the airspace authority.
- DGPS control: ground control points and checkpoints are set around the yard and tied to the railway's reference benchmarks.
- Drone flights: the yard is captured with overlapping images, and with LiDAR where trees or structures hide the ground.
- Processing: the images become an orthomosaic, a surface model and a terrain model with contours.
- Ground survey: rail levels, platform heights and details the drone cannot see are measured with DGPS and total station.
- Drafting: tracks, turnouts, structures and features are drawn in CAD, in the layers and scale the railway specifies.
- Checking and submission: the drawing is verified on site with railway staff, corrected and submitted, with revisions until it is accepted.

### What we deliver

### DPR surveys
A Detailed Project Report is only as good as the survey under it. For railway and road DPRs we provide the survey and mapping inputs the consultant and the authority need to fix the alignment, the structures and the cost:
- Topographic strip survey of the corridor, from drone photogrammetry or LiDAR with DGPS control
- Alignment options compared on the orthomosaic and terrain model
- Longitudinal and cross-sections for earthwork and formation design
- Bridges and drainage: catchments from the terrain model, waterway sections and existing structures
- Land: the corridor laid over khasra (revenue) maps, showing the land and owners affected
- Utilities and obstructions: power lines, pipelines, buildings and other features to be shifted or avoided
- Quantities: earthwork and other quantities measured from the survey data

### Why drones for railway yards
- Safety: the yard is captured from the air, so the survey team spends far less time on or beside running lines.
- Speed: one drone team captures around 5 sq km of survey data in a day, so a yard is flown in hours rather than surveyed over weeks.
- Little disturbance to traffic: flights do not need the line, and the ground work left is short and planned with the station.
- A complete record: the orthomosaic and terrain model stay on file, so later questions can be answered without returning to site.
Accuracy comes from the DGPS ground control and is proved on independent checkpoints. Read more in how accurate a drone survey is and what an Engineering Scale Plan is .

### Frequently asked questions

Q: What is an Engineering Scale Plan (ESP)?
An Engineering Scale Plan is a scaled drawing of a railway station yard or section showing tracks, points and crossings, platforms, buildings and other features in their true positions. Railways use ESPs to plan and approve yard remodelling, new lines and other works.

Q: How does a drone survey help prepare an ESP?
A drone survey with ground control captures the whole yard as an accurate orthomosaic and terrain model in a short time. Drafters then trace tracks, structures and levels from this base, and the field team checks critical details on the ground.

Q: What survey inputs does a DPR need?
A Detailed Project Report usually needs topography of the corridor, existing features and utilities, levels for drainage and earthwork, and land details. Drone, LiDAR and DGPS surveys provide these as drawings and GIS layers.

Q: Does DATA PKT design the project itself?
We provide survey, mapping and design inputs such as drawings and plans. We do not construct projects.

Q: Which railway authorities has DATA PKT worked with?
Our railway clients include Central Railway, North Central Railway, Eastern Railway, Bridge & Roof Co. (India) Ltd and IRCON International, among other railway and metro organisations.

Q: What does an Engineering Scale Plan show?
Tracks and track centres, points and crossings, platforms, foot-over-bridges, level crossings, station buildings and other structures, OHE masts, signals, bridges and culverts, drains, the railway boundary, kilometrage and levels, all in their true positions.

Q: Do you need a traffic block to survey a station yard?
Usually not for the drone flights, which capture the yard from the air. Ground checks of rail levels and details are planned with the station and engineering staff, and kept short.

Q: How accurate is a drone survey for an ESP?
The survey is tied to DGPS ground control points and checked against independent checkpoints, and critical details such as rail levels are measured on the ground. We report the accuracy achieved on the checkpoints with every survey.

Q: In what format are ESPs delivered?
As CAD drawings in the layers and scale the railway asks for, with PDF prints, the orthomosaic, the terrain model and contours, and GIS files on request.

Drones are becoming a crucial component of managing, operating, and preserving wind farms. Using drones instead of traditional inspection makes inspecting rotor blades simple. We can now identify the inside of the rotor blade thanks to developments in the thermal system. Drones cut the number of man-hours and turbine downtime required for maintenance checks by approximately 75%, with inspection times of 15 to 30 minutes per turbine having been proven.
Wind turbine blade inspection methods include both surface and subsurface techniques. Surface inspections use visual technologies like sensors and drones to detect fractures, erosion, lightning, and bird strikes. Early detection enables efficient corrective maintenance. Sub-surface examinations use non-destructive methods such as thermal imaging, ultrasound, and electromagnetic waves to detect structural faults in the blades' internal structure, such as damaged shear webs and bonding erosion. Internal inspections, which require professionals to physically climb into the blades, are limited due to height, safety, and efficiency limits, leaving a considerable fraction uninspected, particularly in offshore wind farms.
Our cutting-edge technology allows us to effectively inspect a wide range of faults in wind turbine blades.

### Frequently asked questions

Q: How are solar plants inspected with drones?
A drone carrying a radiometric thermal camera flies over the plant in good sunlight and records the temperature of every module. Hot spots, faulty strings, bypass diode failures and soiling show up as temperature differences and are mapped to their exact location.

Q: What is a transmission line route survey?
It is a survey of the proposed corridor for a power line to choose the best route and tower positions. Drone and LiDAR data show terrain, obstacles, crossings and clearances, which speeds up route selection and tower spotting.

Q: Can drones inspect live transmission lines and substations?
Yes. Drones inspect towers, insulators, conductors and substation equipment from a safe distance without shutting down the line, using zoom and thermal cameras.

Q: What does a solar thermography report include?
A list of every defect with its type, location, temperature difference and severity, thermal and visual images of each one, and a plant map. See our guide to solar thermography reports for details.

### Frequently asked questions

Q: What is a drone thermal survey?
A drone thermal survey uses an infrared camera on a drone to measure surface temperature across a site. Faults that change temperature, such as failing solar cells, loose electrical joints or water ingress, become visible in the thermal image.

Q: When should a solar thermal inspection be flown?
In clear, steady sunlight with the plant operating, usually around midday. The widely used standard for aerial thermography of PV plants, IEC TS 62446-3, sets a minimum irradiance of 600 W/m² on the modules.

Q: What defects can thermal drones find in a solar plant?
Hot spots and cell cracks, bypass diode faults, open or disconnected strings, junction box overheating, potential induced degradation patterns, and soiling or shading.

Q: What is the difference between radiometric and non-radiometric thermal cameras?
A radiometric camera records a temperature value for every pixel, so each defect can be measured and compared. A non-radiometric camera only shows relative hot and cold areas. Inspection reports need radiometric data.

## LiDAR Drone Survey
Data collection
To collect data, LiDAR uses a specialized sensor that emits pulses of light and measures the time it takes for these signals to bounce back, allowing it to create incredibly detailed 3D maps of land and terrain with pinpoint accuracy.
We utilise state-of-the-art LiDAR sensors mounted on our advanced drones to capture precise 3D data of the survey area. LiDAR technology enables us to collect data points with high accuracy and density, capturing detailed information about terrain elevation, vegetation, buildings, and other features.
Customised Survey Planning
Our team works closely with clients to understand their project requirements and objectives. We design customised survey plans tailored to each project, considering factors such as area coverage, point density, and resolution to ensure optimal data quality and relevance.
Efficient Data Acquisition
Our experienced drone pilots execute the survey missions following carefully planned flight paths. We leverage the flexibility and manoeuvrability of drones to access remote or challenging terrain, maximising data coverage while minimising operational costs and risks.
Data Processing
After data capture, we process the raw LiDAR data using specialised software to generate detailed point clouds. Our team applies sophisticated algorithms to clean, filter, and classify the point cloud data, enhancing its accuracy and usability for various applications.

### Lidar Deliverables
Depending on the particular objectives and specifications of a project, our drone LiDAR (light detection and ranging) technology offers a broad range of outcomes. Our LiDAR outputs offer the potential to provide extremely accurate and detailed topography data that is useful for a wide range of applications across various sectors. The following are potential deliverables we provide:

### Orthomosaic map
Drone photographs are corrected for distortion and seamlessly merged during post-processing to produce a remarkably precise orthomosaic map. Every pixel on this map includes high-quality 2D geographic data (X, Y), allowing exact measurements such as horizontal distances and surface areas to be collected directly.

### 3D Point Cloud
Dense point clouds can be created by processing drone images. Every point in this cloud contains geographic coordinates (X, Y, Z) and colour information, providing an extremely precise model for measuring lengths (horizontal and vertical), as well as areas and volumes.

### DSM
A DSM captures ‘the natural and built features' on the earth's surface. DSMs represent the bare earth and all of its above-ground features. Drone images can also be used to create DSM models of the area. Each pixel contains 2D information (X, Y) and the altitude (Z value) of the highest point for this position.

### DTM
DTM's (Digital Terrain Model) are detected using aerial photography at low heights with a geometrically calibrated camera. This enables the drone to obtain all the heights of the surveyed terrain. In these models, each pixel stores 2.5D information, including the X, Y, and Z values corresponding to the highest altitude.

### Contour map
We can obtain a greater understanding of the area the drone photographed by using a contour line map that can be created using the DTM or DSM model with specific contour intervals, depending on the requirements of the project.

### Volume Calculations
Drone LiDAR can be used to calculate the volume of materials, such as soil, rock, and gravel, with a high degree of accuracy. This information can be used for a range of applications, including mining, construction, and environmental studies.

### Frequently asked questions

Q: What is a drone LiDAR survey?
LiDAR sends laser pulses from the drone and measures their return to build a dense 3D point cloud of the ground and everything on it. Because some pulses pass through gaps in vegetation, LiDAR can map the ground surface under trees.

Q: When should I choose LiDAR over photogrammetry?
Choose LiDAR for corridors and sites with vegetation, for power lines and for very detailed terrain. Photogrammetry is usually more economical for open ground and gives a true-colour orthomosaic. Many projects use both.

Q: What deliverables come from a LiDAR survey?
A classified point cloud (ground, vegetation, buildings, wires), a digital terrain model, a digital surface model, contours and cross-sections, in formats ready for CAD and GIS.

Q: How accurate is drone LiDAR?
Accuracy depends on the sensor, flying height and ground control. Survey-grade drone LiDAR checked against ground control typically reaches a few centimetres vertically on hard surfaces.

## Drone Photogrammetry
At DATA PKT Infra & Geomatics, we help with the following photogrammetry steps:

### Data Acquisition
Planning and Preparation
- Define project objectives and requirements.
- Identify survey area and assess potential obstacles.
- Determine optimal flight path and altitude.
- Ensure 80% image overlap for accurate orthophoto creation.
- Check weather conditions and obtain necessary permits.
Equipment Setup
- Ensure drone and camera are in good working condition.
- Calibrate drone sensors and cameras.
- Install and configure additional hardware (e.g., GPS).
Camera Model Optimization
Camera calibration calculates camera specifications using photos of a 3D object with a geometrical pattern (e.g., checkerboard). Calibration types include Full, Field, Self, and Auto.
- Full calibration sets up a specific camera calibration project.
- Field calibration optimizes the camera during normal project processing.
- Self-calibration adjusts camera parameters for each photo individually.
- Auto calibration integrates with Smart Orientation for field calibration.

### GCP (Ground control points)
Ground control points (or GCPs) are known-coordinated places on the ground. GCPs are points that a surveyor can precisely locate in an aerial mapping survey, allowing enormous regions to be correctly mapped with just a few known coordinates.
Anything that may be clearly identified in the photos can be used as a ground control point. They usually resemble little checkerboard pieces. The form eliminates any doubt about where a ground control point is.

#### Is it always necessary to use GCP?
GCPs have long been used in aerial mapping operations. However, as new technologies are introduced to the market, this is changing.
Ground control points do not significantly increase accuracy when utilising an RTK or PPK capable drone.
We always advocate using GCPs if your drone does not have RTK or PPK capability.
While skipping ground control points may produce absolutely acceptable results, your reconstruction may lack the necessary scale, orientation, or absolute location data. The GCPs, RTK, and PPK geotags can aid in the verification of the reconstruction's correctness.

#### The difference between GCP, Automatic and Manual tie points
GCP are known as Ground control points. These are known coordinates points on ground & can be known using instruments like DGPS & Total-Station.
Automatic ties are points that appear in numerous photographs. This is something that the program can detect. They are frequently used as common spots in picture stitching.
Any immediately identifiable place that appears in several photos, such as the corner of a building or a road, can be used as a manual tie point.
Manual tie points can assist in enhancing a project's relative accuracy, but they can't help with absolute precision because their location in space isn't known.

### Flight Execution
- Conduct a pre-flight check to verify all systems are functioning correctly.
- Launch the drone and follow the planned flight path, adjusting altitude and camera settings as needed.
- Capture overlapping aerial images with sufficient ground coverage and detail.
- Maintain communication and monitor the drone's position and battery life throughout the flight.
- Ensure the drone returns to the home point or a safe landing location with ample battery reserve.
- Post-flight inspection to assess drone condition and review any captured data for quality.
- Transfer and back up all aerial images and data to a secure storage location.
- Analyze the captured images to create a detailed map or 3D model of the surveyed area.
- Download and back up all captured images and flight data immediately after landing.
- Regularly check the weather conditions and adjust the flight plan if necessary.

### Data Processing
- Transfer the captured imagery to a computer or processing device.
- Use specialized photogrammetry software to stitch together the individual images into a cohesive mosaic.
- Apply algorithms to triangulate image features and generate a dense point cloud representing the surveyed area.
- Generate orthomosaics, digital surface models (DSMs), and other derived products from the processed data.
- Validate the accuracy of the generated models by comparing them with ground control points (GCPs) or known reference data.
- Perform quality checks on the orthomosaics and DSMs to identify and correct any artifacts or inconsistencies.
- Export the processed data into various formats suitable for different applications and software platforms.
- Integrate the geospatial data with GIS software for further analysis and visualization.

### Data Quality Control and Analysis
- Validate the accuracy and completeness of the generated 3D models and maps.
- Conduct any necessary adjustments or corrections to improve the quality of the data.
- Perform measurements, analysis, and interpretation of the photogrammetric outputs to extract relevant information.
- Share the validated models and maps with stakeholders for feedback and further insights.
- Use the extracted information to support decision-making processes in relevant projects or applications.
- Document the methodologies and workflows used in the photogrammetric process for reproducibility and future reference.
- Train team members or clients on how to utilize the photogrammetric data effectively.
- Stay updated with advancements in photogrammetry techniques and software to continuously improve the quality and efficiency of data processing.

### Deliverables

### Orthomosaic map
Drone photographs are corrected for distortion and seamlessly merged during post-processing to produce a remarkably precise orthomosaic map. Every pixel on this map includes high 2D geographic data (X, Y), allowing exact measurements such as horizontal distances and surface areas to be collected directly.

### 3D Point Cloud
Drone images processed to create dense point clouds yield precise models with geographic coordinates (X, Y, Z) and color data for accurate measurements of horizontal and vertical lengths, areas, and volumes. These point clouds offer highly detailed representations, enhancing measurement precision in various applications.

### DSM
A DSM captures the natural and built features' on the Earth's surface. DSMs represent the bare- earth and all of its above-ground features. Drone images can also be used to create DSM models of the area. Each pixel contains 2D information (X, Y) and the altitude (Z value) of the highest point for this position.

### DTM
DTM's (Digital Terrain Model) are detected using aerial photography at low heights with a geometrically calibrated camera. This enables the drone to obtain all the heights of the surveyed terrain. In these models, each pixel stores 2.5D information, including the X, Y, and Z values corresponding to the highest altitude.

### Contour map
By utilizing a contour line map created from a DTM or DSM model with specific contour intervals, we can gain a deeper understanding of the area photographed by the drone. The contour intervals can be adjusted according to the project's requirements, enhancing the detail and accuracy of the analysis.

### 3D Textured Mash
A 3D textured mesh generated from drone imagery offers a detailed and accurate representation of the site's surfaces, walls, and edges. This model enhances understanding by providing a comprehensive view of the area, essential for precise analysis and project planning.

We achieve up to 99% accuracy in our results, employing advanced machine learning techniques for precise yield estimation, volumetric measurements, and more.

### Frequently asked questions

Q: What is drone photogrammetry?
Photogrammetry builds maps and 3D models from many overlapping aerial photos. Processing software matches points across the photos to produce an orthomosaic, a surface model and a 3D mesh.

Q: How accurate is drone photogrammetry?
With RTK or PPK positioning and well-placed ground control points, drone photogrammetry typically reaches a few centimetres of accuracy. The ground sample distance (GSD), which depends on camera and flying height, sets the level of detail.

Q: What is a ground control point (GCP)?
A GCP is a marked point on the ground whose coordinates are measured with DGPS. GCPs tie the drone map to real-world coordinates, and independent checkpoints are used to prove the final accuracy.

Q: What file formats will I receive?
Usually GeoTIFF orthomosaics and elevation models, contours and features in DWG or DXF, GIS layers as shapefiles or GeoPackage, and point clouds in LAS or LAZ.

Using a drone, DATA PKT assists in optimising the following processes throughout the mining development phase:-

#### Haulage Road Optimization
A haul road is a type of road in the mining industry used to transport heavy and bulky materials by haul trucks. It is sometimes referred to as a haulage road or a haul track.
Material hauling accounts for a significant portion of a mine's expenses. A safe transportation system is made possible by well-designed and maintained roads, which immediately cut cycle times, fuel consumption, tyre prices, and overall cost per tonne transported.
Drones are capable of performing a range of activities connected to haulage roads, including precision mapping, time-sensitive land surveys, and quick road inspections. Drones are necessary for the long-term and economic management of transportation infrastructure and road upkeep.

#### Surveying and Mapping
Traditional surveying techniques require careful measuring, planning, and preparation, which adds delay to the data collection process. Drones, on the other hand, can gather all of this data in a very short amount of time. A conventional survey would take 70% longer than one using drones. In addition, as compared to traditional surveys, drone surveys need half the amount of labour.

#### Tailings dam monitoring
Most notably in metallurgical or coal mines, tailings dams are a familiar sight. They may cover entire square kilometres and are built of earth. They act as a garbage repository for all the contaminated byproducts of mining activities. When you decide to use a drone to monitor your tailings dam, you instantly cut down on the dangers of surveying staff by cutting the likelihood of people entering unsafe regions by 48%. Drone surveying is possible using just line-of-sight distance. There is no longer a need for them to remain so near to the area's harmful chemicals and dust.

#### Stockpile management and calculation
Stockpile management is crucial for minimizing environmental impact and ensuring regulatory compliance in mining and construction activities. By implementing erosion control measures such as proper covering, grading, and vegetation, companies can mitigate the risk of sediment flow from soil stockpiles, preserving nearby waterways and ecosystems. Moreover, stockpile management becomes imperative when dealing with erodible materials, as it helps prevent soil loss, contamination, and potential hazards to surrounding areas.
DATA PKT revolutionizes stockpile management by providing comprehensive solutions tailored to the specific needs of miners. Through advanced technology integration, DATA PKT enables transparent operations by providing stakeholders with real-time access to crucial data and analytics. Enhanced inventory management ensures optimal utilization of resources while minimizing waste and redundancy. Real-time quarry monitoring allows for proactive decision-making and risk mitigation, enhancing safety and operational efficiency. Additionally, the use of drones for stockpile evaluation provides accurate volumetric measurements, improving planning and forecasting capabilities. Overall, DATA PKT empowers miners to streamline their stockpile management processes, leading to cost savings, time efficiencies, and sustainable operations.
Reclamation of mined land is the process of restoring it to the condition it was in before mining. When you restore land, you are minimizing the negative environmental consequences of mining. Reforestation and new development are the most typical methods of reclamation.
The most accurate approach to predict how much work is left to do and when reclamation will start is to use a drone, which also aids in tracking extraction progress and material movement. Aerial surveys employing numerous drone flights are the quickest and most reliable way to get this data.

#### Benefits of using drones in the mining sector:-
Site Safety Management
Mining sites feature volatile sections with rugged terrain where safety is of the utmost priority. Drones can give precise, high-quality photogrammetric data of mines, which is subsequently turned into digital elevation and surface models. This allows for improved management and task implementation of mining sites
Automated Inspection
Compared to traditional methods, drones with built-in automation assess mining blast sites without endangering human lives. The expense associated with employing significant human resources can be avoided by automating mine inspection using drones. Drones gather an enormous quantity of data that may be used to create othomosaic maps to provide an updated perspective of vast tracts of land.

DATA PKT drones monitor mining sites with high-quality embedded sensors and give real-time, cost-effective data access. Deep mining tunnels that are inaccessible manually can be monitored by UAVs. This aids in site surveillance and the discovery of any leaks that can endanger human life. Real-time data access guarantees that corrective actions be implemented as soon as problems are found.
Mine Survey Using Lidar
The use of LiDAR (light detection and ranging) for measuring and inspecting mining pits assists in the creation of precise topographical maps of mining operations. Drones integrated with LiDAR sensors to aid in obtaining precise information about the steepness of embankments and unstable ground foundations. While keeping on-site surveyors secure, drones assist surveyors to navigate topographically difficult areas.
Volume Calculation
Volume calculations are important in mining as it helps in determining the cost and efficiency of machines and mining methods. Traditionally, RTK-GPS systems are required to be installed, the installation can be life-threatening for the miner, therefore Digital terrain modelling(DTM) can be used for volume calculations with the help of Drones.

### Frequently asked questions

Q: How are stockpile volumes measured with drones?
The drone maps the stockpiles and the software builds a 3D surface. Volumes are calculated against a base surface, which is faster and safer than walking the pile with a survey instrument.

Q: How often should a mine be surveyed by drone?
Many mines fly monthly or quarterly so that excavation, dumping and stock figures can be compared period by period. The frequency depends on how fast the site changes and reporting needs.

Q: Can drones map active pits safely?
Yes. The drone collects data from the air, so surveyors do not need to approach unstable faces or work near moving equipment.

Q: What mining outputs are typical?
Orthomosaics, terrain models, contours, pit and dump boundaries, volume reports, haul road profiles and change-detection maps between surveys.

### Frequently asked questions

Q: How are drones used in water resources projects?
Drones survey canals, rivers, embankments and reservoir shorelines to produce terrain models, cross-sections and maps for design, repair and monitoring.

Q: Can a drone survey measure underwater depth?
Standard drone cameras do not see through water, so depth is measured by a bathymetry survey with an echo sounder. The two datasets are merged into one model of the banks and the bed.

Q: What outputs help canal design and maintenance?
Longitudinal and cross sections, bank and bed levels, contour maps, encroachment mapping and orthomosaics of the canal corridor.

Q: Can drones help with flood studies?
Yes. An accurate terrain model of the catchment or floodplain is a key input to flood modelling and planning embankments and drainage.

## Bathymetry Survey

### High-Resolution Mapping
- Sonar Technology Drones equipped with sonar sensors emit sound waves that travel through the water and bounce back after hitting the seabed, lakebed, or riverbed. The time taken for the sound waves to return is used to calculate the depth of the water at various points.
- GPS Integration High-precision GPS systems onboard the drones ensure that each depth measurement is accurately georeferenced, allowing for the creation of detailed spatial maps.
- Depth Contours The collected depth data is processed to generate depth contours, which are lines connecting points of equal depth. These contours help in understanding the variations in underwater terrain.
- Feature Identification Detailed maps can highlight specific underwater features such as trenches, ridges, and submerged objects, providing valuable information for various applications.
- Environmental Studies High-resolution maps aid in the study of aquatic habitats, helping to monitor and protect ecosystems.
- Engineering Projects Accurate topographical data is crucial for planning and constructing underwater structures like bridges, pipelines, and docks.
- Navigation Mariners use these maps to navigate safely, avoiding underwater hazards.
- Precision and Detail High-resolution mapping provides an unparalleled level of detail, which is essential for accurate analysis and decision-making.
- Efficiency Drones can cover large areas quickly, significantly reducing the time and cost compared to traditional survey methods..

### 3D Modeling
Data Collection and Integration
- Multi-Angle Scanning Drones perform multiple passes over the survey area, collecting data from different angles. This multi-angle approach ensures that all features are captured accurately.
- Integrated Sensors Alongside sonar, drones can be equipped with additional sensors like LiDAR (Light Detection and Ranging) and high-resolution cameras to enhance the detail and accuracy of the models.
Model Generation
- Point Cloud Creation The data collected is used to create a point cloud, a set of data points in a three-dimensional coordinate system representing the underwater terrain.
- Surface Reconstruction Advanced software processes the point cloud to generate a 3D surface model, which can be textured and colored to reflect the actual appearance of the seabed.
Applications
- Visualization 3D models provide an immersive view of the underwater environment, useful for presentations, education, and stakeholder engagement.
- Simulation and Analysis Engineers and scientists can use these models for simulations, such as predicting the impact of construction projects on the underwater landscape.
Advantages:
- Enhanced Understanding 3D models offer a more intuitive and comprehensive view of the underwater environment compared to traditional 2D maps.
- Versatility These models can be used in various software applications for further analysis, virtual reality experiences, and detailed planning.

### Coastal and Shoreline Surveys
Tracking shoreline erosion is a critical process that provides valuable insights into the dynamic changes occurring along coastlines. By monitoring erosion patterns and shoreline positions over time, authorities can develop informed coastal management and defense strategies, enabling proactive measures to mitigate the impacts of erosion and protect vulnerable communities. Moreover, habitat mapping is a complementary component of coastal conservation, involving the surveying of sensitive habitats like coral reefs, seagrass beds, and mangrove forests.
This process allows scientists to pinpoint areas in need of protection or restoration, and develop targeted initiatives to preserve these ecosystems. The integration of shoreline erosion monitoring and habitat mapping fosters a comprehensive understanding of coastal dynamics, supporting a holistic approach to coastal management that balances human needs with environmental stewardship. This multi-faceted approach enables the development of effective conservation strategies, ensuring the long-term health and resilience of coastal ecosystems, and the communities that depend on them. By combining these two essential components, we can better manage and protect our valuable coastal resources for future generations.

### Environmental Monitoring and Assessment
Monitoring water quality is a crucial process that involves collecting data on various parameters such as temperature, pH, and turbidity, in conjunction with depth measurements. This comprehensive approach provides a detailed understanding of the physical and chemical characteristics of water bodies, enabling the identification of potential pollution sources and areas of concern. Additionally, sediment transport studies are essential for understanding the dynamics of sediment movement in rivers, lakes, and coastal areas.
By analyzing sediment distribution and movement, scientists can gain valuable insights into the processes that shape our waterways and coastlines. This knowledge is critical for managing sediment transport, preventing erosion and sedimentation, and mitigating the impacts of human activities on aquatic ecosystems. The combination of water quality monitoring and sediment transport studies enables a holistic understanding of aquatic systems, supporting effective management and conservation strategies. By monitoring water quality and sediment transport dynamics, we can better protect and preserve our vital water resources, ensuring the health and sustainability of aquatic ecosystems and the communities that depend on them.

### Infrastructure Planning and Inspection
Before breaking ground on infrastructure projects like bridges, piers, and underwater pipelines, site assessments are crucial to ensure optimal placement and design. These pre-construction surveys involve thorough investigations of the site conditions, including the seafloor, water depth, and surrounding environment. By gathering this data, engineers can design infrastructure that is tailored to the specific site conditions, minimizing risks and ensuring successful project outcomes. Additionally, regular structural inspections are essential for evaluating the condition of existing underwater infrastructure, such as dams, levees, and seawalls.
These inspections involve a thorough examination of the structure's condition, identifying any damage, deterioration, or required maintenance. This enables proactive repairs and maintenance, preventing catastrophic failures and ensuring the continued safety and functionality of these critical infrastructure assets. By conducting site assessments and structural inspections, engineers can ensure the longevity and integrity of underwater infrastructure, supporting public safety, economic growth, and environmental sustainability.

### Flood Risk Management
Mapping floodplains and assessing flood risk is a critical process that helps identify areas vulnerable to flooding, enabling informed decision-making for flood mitigation strategies. Floodplain mapping involves creating detailed maps of flood-prone areas, taking into account factors such as topography, hydrology, and storm patterns. This information is essential for developing effective flood risk management plans, ensuring that communities are prepared for potential flooding events. Additionally, evaluating the effectiveness of flood defense structures like levees and barriers is crucial for ensuring their ability to protect against flooding.
Flood defense assessments involve a thorough examination of these structures, identifying areas of strength and weakness, and recommending upgrades or repairs as needed. By combining floodplain mapping and flood defense assessments, communities can proactively manage flood risk, reduce the impact of flooding events, and protect lives, property, and infrastructure. This integrated approach enables a comprehensive understanding of flood risk, supporting proactive strategies to mitigate the effects of flooding and promote community resilience.

### Aquaculture
Conducting fish farm surveys is essential for identifying optimal locations for fish cages, ensuring that aquaculture activities are sustainable and minimally impactful on the surrounding environment. These surveys involve assessing water quality, sea floor topography, and other factors to determine the best placement for fish cages, maximizing growth and minimizing environmental footprint. Additionally, environmental impact studies are crucial for understanding the effects of aquaculture activities on the marine ecosystem.
These studies involve monitoring water quality, sedimentation, and biodiversity, as well as assessing the potential for disease and parasite transfer between farmed and wild fish populations. By conducting regular environmental impact studies, fish farms can proactively mitigate any negative effects, ensuring a sustainable and environmentally friendly operation. The combination of fish farm surveys and environmental impact studies enables a holistic approach to aquaculture management, supporting the long-term health of both the fish farming industry and the marine environment. This integrated approach promotes responsible and sustainable aquaculture practices, ensuring a balance between food production and environmental stewardship.

### Archaeological Surveys
Uncovering the secrets of the past requires precise location and mapping of underwater archaeological sites, such as shipwrecks and submerged settlements. Underwater archaeology involves the use of advanced technologies to identify and document these sites with high accuracy, preserving valuable historical and cultural information. By creating detailed maps and 3D models of these sites, researchers can reconstruct the past and gain insights into the lives of ancient civilizations. This work is crucial for understanding historical events, cultural exchange, and the impact of human activity on the environment.
Moreover, precise mapping enables the monitoring of site conditions, supporting conservation efforts and protecting these valuable cultural resources for future generations. The application of advanced technologies in underwater archaeology has revolutionized the field, enabling the discovery and exploration of previously inaccessible sites. By exploring and preserving our underwater cultural heritage, we can deepen our understanding of human history and promote a sense of shared identity and responsibility for our collective past.

### Frequently asked questions

Q: What is a bathymetry survey?
A bathymetry survey measures the depth and shape of the bed of a river, reservoir, lake or canal, usually with an echo sounder linked to GNSS positioning.

Q: Why combine bathymetry with a drone survey?
The drone maps banks and dry areas, and bathymetry maps the bed under water. Together they give one continuous terrain model for design, capacity and siltation studies.

Q: What can bathymetry data be used for?
Reservoir capacity and siltation studies, dredging volumes, river training and bridge design, intake and outfall design, and flood modelling.

Q: What are the typical deliverables?
Depth points, a bed surface model, contours, cross-sections and capacity tables, in CAD and GIS formats.

Q: Do drone flights in cities need permission?
Yes. Flights must follow India's drone rules and airspace zones; flights in yellow or red zones need prior permission. Survey plans are made around these limits.

#### Hyperspectral based species mapping
Utilizing hyperspectral sensors on drones enables precise species mapping by capturing spectral signatures. These sensors detect unique wavelengths reflected by various vegetation types, aiding in accurate species identification. Data processing techniques analyse spectral information to map species distribution and abundance. This approach offers efficient and non-invasive monitoring of ecosystems for biodiversity conservation and management.
Leveraging drone technology with hyperspectral sensors enhances ecological research and environmental monitoring capabilities.

#### Crop health and stress analysis
Our services, equipped with multispectral or thermal imaging sensors, can capture detailed aerial imagery of agricultural fields. This data helps farmers monitor crop health and detect pests, diseases, and nutrient deficiencies, allowing for timely intervention and optimised crop management practices. Our top-notch drones furnished with Multispectral camera sensors can identify disease and stress in the initial stages, sometimes before it is even evident from the ground or with standard colour cameras. Our drone surveys also provide real-time imagery of the fields for precision agriculture. The data obtained is processed and analysed during Irrigation Monitoring, Crop Health Monitoring, and other fundamental elements to encourage farmers to focus on treatment plans.
Using RGB sensors, crop variability can be assessed using the visual atmospheric resistance index (VARI); however, NIR and multispectral sensors are better at detecting and distinguishing crop stress using the Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI). Normalized Difference Red Edge (NDRE) is also often used in conjunction with multispectral data, offering more accurate crop health analysis in later growing stages. Thermal cameras can also be used to determine crop water stress by picking up variations in temperature within a crop, indicating irrigation issues.
Plant health algorithms explained
Healthy plants reflect light differently than unhealthy plants. This allows us to pick out plants that may be under stress from disease, pests, dehydration, etc. This is done by using plant health algorithms such as the Visual Atmospheric Resistance Index (VARI), Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI), and Normalized Difference Red Edge (NDRE). These algorithms are the most commonly used for agricultural purposes.
VARI was designed to be used with RGB sensors and measures how green an image is. Healthy plants tend to reflect more green light and less red light. This allows VARI to highlight areas where less green light is being reflected, suggesting plant stress.
NDVI was designed to be used with NIR and multispectral cameras and measures the ratio between NIR and red being reflected from a plant. Plants that are healthy should be absorbing red light for photosynthesis and reflecting more NIR than stressed plants, allowing for this algorithm to indicate the health of plants.
NDRE was designed to be used as an index for multispectral cameras and measures the ratio between NIR and red edge being reflected from a plant. This algorithm is typically better in the later growth stages of crops, as Red edge is absorbed less than red light by surface leaves, giving a better overview of plant health when plant canopies are dense. NDRE gives a picture of leaf chlorophyll content, which is a good indicator of foliar nitrogen levels

### Frequently asked questions

Q: What is NDVI?
NDVI (Normalised Difference Vegetation Index) is a measure of plant health calculated from red and near-infrared light. Healthy vegetation reflects more near-infrared, so stressed areas show up clearly on an NDVI map.

Q: What camera is used for crop health mapping?
A multispectral camera that records near-infrared and other bands as well as visible light. Hyperspectral cameras record many narrow bands for research-level analysis.

Q: What can drone maps do for a farm or plantation?
Show crop stress and variation across fields, map field boundaries and drainage, count plants or trees, and help plan inputs where they are needed.

Q: Is drone mapping useful for agricultural research?
Yes. Repeated multispectral flights give consistent, measurable data on plots over the season.

## Drone Survey for Oil and Gas
Upstream
Midstream
Downstream
This process includes determining possible geographical sites, undertaking surveys, drilling and exploring, and producing crude oil and gas. Drones have the potential to transform this previously time-consuming, manual procedure into an efficient and accurate one in the following ways:

#### Provide real-time data for all the steps.
- Thermal sensors and cameras on drones provide real-time data for identifying optimal transfer routes and relevant infrastructure during midstream operations.
- During construction, managers can remotely supervise progress using real-time video feeds from drones, facilitating timely decision-making and project oversight.
- Designers can monitor work progress in real-time to ensure adherence to plans and identify any need for adjustments or modifications.
- Drones assist in predictive maintenance by continuously gathering real-time vibration data about potential issues such as leakage and corrosion, enabling proactive maintenance actions to be taken.
- Real-time relay of data via drones bridges the gap between data collection and action, allowing authorities to respond promptly to potential problems, thereby enhancing output and productivity.
Midstream refers to the process of transporting crude oil and gas obtained upstream through pipelines, barges, or oil tankers for downstream processing and storage. Long pipelines that may exist above ground or underwater, transport issues, or surplus storage, all of which necessitate secure storage during treatment and subsequent transit as needed.
Midstream activities involve transporting crude oil and gas from upstream production sites to downstream processing facilities and storage locations. Infrastructure for midstream operations includes pipelines, barges, and oil tankers, which transport the resources over long distances, above ground or underwater. Secure storage is essential during midstream processes to address transport issues, accommodate surplus storage needs, and ensure efficient treatment and transit of crude oil and gas
- Infrastructure for midstream operations also encompasses storage facilities such as tanks, terminals, and depots, strategically located along transportation routes to facilitate smooth transitions between different modes of transportation and accommodate fluctuations in demand.
- - Midstream activities play a critical role in ensuring the reliability and security of the energy supply chain, requiring stringent safety measures and environmental regulations to mitigate risks associated with the transportation and storage of crude oil and gas.
Standing at the conclusion of the cycle, downstream serves as a link between oil and gas businesses and end consumers (B2B, B2C & B2G). At this stage, crude oil and raw natural gas are refined to produce end products such as gasoline, jet fuel, heating oil, natural gas, LPG, and other petrochemicals.
As downstream is closest to the supply chain, a significant amount of people and other resources are expended to ensure that the end product is delivered on time and in an environmentally friendly manner. Industrial leftovers must also be appropriately disposed of so that they do not pose a risk to others.

#### Here, drones can help in the following manner in midstream and downstream
Pipeline Inspections
The inspection of pipelines is one of the most important applications of drones in the oil and gas industry. Drones provide an aerial perspective that allows for comprehensive analysis of pipeline conditions without having to shut down the pipeline. A pipeline inspection drone can spot environmental encroachments, physical damage, corrosion, leaks, and spills.
Gas Flare Stack Inspections
Gas flare stacks are used to burn off waste gases from oil and gas production. Flare stack inspections are critical to maintaining safety and compliance. A drone can capture high-resolution images and thermal imaging to detect leaks, gas combustion, and other potential safety hazards. Through drone inspections, maintenance checks can be done without having to shut down production.
Power Line Inspections
Power lines are critical to the oil and gas industry. Drones can provide effective visual inspections and thermographic imaging to detect damage, wear and tear, and hot spots on power lines. Inspections can be done much more efficiently than traditional methods, reducing costs and minimising safety risks.
Oil Rig Inspections
Drones can inspect oil rig platforms, derricks, and equipment. With infrared imaging, drones can detect potential equipment failures and cracks that might not be visible from the ground. A drone inspection of drilling platforms increases cost-effectiveness, efficacy, and safety.
Tank Inspections
Tanks are crucial elements in the oil and gas industry. Routine inspections are necessary to detect leaks, surface corrosion, or other damage to the tank. Drones can detect surface level changes, leaks, and other issues that might not be visible to the naked eye. A drone inspection of tanks reduces safety risks and maintenance costs.
